text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To better understand your condition, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen with specific movements or head positions?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with C8-T1 radiculopathy.

The patient's progressive weakness and paresthesias in both hands, combined with a one-year history of neck/arm pain, are highly suggestive of cervical spine pathology compressing the cord and nerve roots. Given his age and chronic symptoms, this is likely degenerative changes (cervical spondylosis) rather than post-traumatic given the 3-year gap since his accident. I am proceeding with imaging to confirm the level and severity of compression.
